docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Greet people and say goodbye in formal and informal ways.
- Introduce yourself and other people.
- Ask for and give personal information (name, age, country, job).
- Use the verb "to be" and simple question words with confidence.

🔍 Warm-up
Imagine you meet a new classmate. What do you say first? Read this short dialogue:
- Hello! My name is Leila. What's your name?
- Hi Leila. I'm Karim. Nice to meet you.
- Nice to meet you too!
This lesson helps you build conversations exactly like this one.

I. Greetings and goodbyes

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 660 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="330" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Formal vs Informal Greetings</text>
<rect x="30" y="45" width="285" height="34" rx="8" fill="#16a34a"/>
<text x="172" y="67" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Informal — friends, family</text>
<text x="172" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Hi! Hello! Hey!</text>
<text x="172" y="120" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">How's it going?</text>
<text x="172" y="140" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Bye! See you later!</text>
<rect x="345" y="45" width="285" height="34" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="487" y="67" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Formal — teachers, adults</text>
<text x="487" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Good morning / afternoon / evening</text>
<text x="487" y="120" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">How are you?</text>
<text x="487" y="140" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Goodbye. Good night.</text>
<rect x="60" y="175" width="540" height="60" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="330" y="197" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">Careful: "Good night" is NOT a greeting</text>
<text x="330" y="216" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">Use it only to say goodbye at night. To greet at night, say "Good evening".</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📘 Rule (functions)
We choose our greeting depending on WHO we talk to and WHEN.
Informal (friends, family, classmates): Hi! Hello! Hey!
Formal (teachers, adults, strangers): Good morning. Good afternoon. Good evening.
Saying goodbye: Goodbye. Bye. See you later. See you tomorrow. Good night (only when going to sleep or leaving at night).

📏 Form: asking how someone is
- How are you? — I'm fine, thank you. And you?
- How are you doing? — Very well, thanks.
- How's it going? — Not bad, thanks.

👀 Note
"Good night" is NOT a greeting. We use it only to say goodbye late in the evening or before sleeping. To greet someone at night we still say "Good evening".

II. Introducing yourself and others
📏 Form (introducing yourself)
- My name is + name. / I'm + name.
- I am + age (years old).
- I'm from + country/city.
- I live in + place.

✏️ Worked examples
- My name is Sami. I'm twelve years old. I'm from Tunisia. I live in Sfax.
- Hello, I'm Nour. I am eleven. I come from Bizerte.

📏 Form (introducing another person)
- This is + name. He / She is + information.
- Meet my friend Amine. He is thirteen.

🛠️ Method: a full self-introduction

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 700 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="350" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Five Steps of a Self-Introduction</text>
<g font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">
<rect x="15" y="55" width="122" height="60" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="76" y="80" text-anchor="middle">1. Greet</text>
<rect x="150" y="55" width="122" height="60" rx="8" fill="#16a34a"/>
<text x="211" y="80" text-anchor="middle">2. Name</text>
<rect x="285" y="55" width="122" height="60" rx="8" fill="#e11d48"/>
<text x="346" y="80" text-anchor="middle">3. Age</text>
<rect x="420" y="55" width="122" height="60" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="481" y="80" text-anchor="middle">4. From</text>
<rect x="555" y="55" width="122" height="60" rx="8" fill="#16a34a"/>
<text x="616" y="80" text-anchor="middle">5. Close</text>
</g>
<g font-size="10.5" fill="#ffffff">
<text x="76" y="98" text-anchor="middle">"Hello!"</text>
<text x="211" y="98" text-anchor="middle">"My name is..."</text>
<text x="346" y="98" text-anchor="middle">"I am ... years old"</text>
<text x="481" y="98" text-anchor="middle">"I'm from..."</text>
<text x="616" y="98" text-anchor="middle">"Nice to meet you"</text>
</g>
<line x1="137" y1="85" x2="150" y2="85" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="272" y1="85" x2="285" y2="85" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="407" y1="85" x2="420" y2="85" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="542" y1="85" x2="555" y2="85" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="350" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">"Hello! My name is Sami. I'm twelve years old. I'm from Tunisia. Nice to meet you."</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
Step 1 — Greet: Hello / Good morning.
Step 2 — Give your name: My name is...
Step 3 — Give your age: I am ... years old.
Step 4 — Say where you are from: I'm from...
Step 5 — Close politely: Nice to meet you.

III. The verb "to be"

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 640 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="320" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">The Verb "To Be" — Present</text>
<rect x="40" y="42" width="180" height="28" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="130" y="61" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Subject</text>
<rect x="220" y="42" width="180" height="28" fill="#16a34a"/>
<text x="310" y="61" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Affirmative</text>
<rect x="400" y="42" width="200" height="28" fill="#e11d48"/>
<text x="500" y="61" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Short form</text>
<g font-size="12" fill="currentColor">
<text x="130" y="90" text-anchor="middle">I</text><text x="310" y="90" text-anchor="middle">am</text><text x="500" y="90" text-anchor="middle">I'm</text>
<text x="130" y="112" text-anchor="middle">you/we/they</text><text x="310" y="112" text-anchor="middle">are</text><text x="500" y="112" text-anchor="middle">you're / we're / they're</text>
<text x="130" y="134" text-anchor="middle">he/she/it</text><text x="310" y="134" text-anchor="middle">is</text><text x="500" y="134" text-anchor="middle">he's / she's / it's</text>
</g>
<rect x="60" y="165" width="520" height="55" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="320" y="185" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">Negative: am not / isn't / aren't</text>
<text x="320" y="204" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">She isn't from Tunis. They aren't at home.</text>
<rect x="60" y="230" width="520" height="55" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="320" y="250" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">Age uses "to be", never "to have"</text>
<text x="320" y="269" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">I am twelve (years old). NOT "I have twelve years".</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📘 Rule (grammar)
"To be" is the most important verb for personal information.
📏 Forms (affirmative)
- I am (I'm)
- You are (you're)
- He / She / It is (he's / she's / it's)
- We / You / They are (we're / they're)

📏 Negative
- I am not (I'm not), you are not (aren't), he is not (isn't), they are not (aren't).

📏 Questions
- Am I...? Are you...? Is he/she/it...? Are we/they...?
- Short answers: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.

✏️ Worked examples
- Are you from Tunis? — No, I'm not. I'm from Gabès.
- Is she your sister? — Yes, she is.
- They are not at home.

⚠️ Common mistakes
- Do not use "have" for age in English. Wrong: I have twelve years. Right: I am twelve (years old).
- Do not forget the verb "to be". Wrong: I from Tunisia. Right: I am from Tunisia.
- "It's" (it is) is different from "its" (belonging to it).

IV. Asking for personal information
📘 Rule (question words)
- What...? for names and things: What's your name? What's your phone number?
- How old...? for age: How old are you?
- Where...? for place: Where are you from? Where do you live?
- What...do...? for jobs: What do you do? / What's your job?

📏 Form (common questions and answers)
- What's your name? — My name is...
- How old are you? — I'm twelve.
- Where are you from? — I'm from Tunisia.
- What's your favourite... ? — My favourite colour is blue.

✏️ Worked dialogue
- Good morning. What's your name, please?
- Good morning. My name is Rania.
- How old are you, Rania?
- I'm eleven years old.
- Where do you live?
- I live in Monastir. Nice to meet you.
- Nice to meet you too.

👀 Note
"What's" = "What is". We use short forms (contractions) a lot in speaking: I'm, you're, he's, what's, it's. They make English sound natural and friendly.

⚠️ More common mistakes
1. Answering the wrong question: How old are you? — Wrong: I'm fine. Right: I'm twelve.
2. Capital letters: names, countries and languages always start with a capital: Tunisia, Karim, English.
3. Forgetting the question mark at the end of a question.

⭐ Recap
- Choose formal or informal greetings depending on the person.
- Introduce yourself with name, age, and where you are from.
- Master the verb "to be": am / is / are.
- Use "I am" (not "I have") to give your age.
- Question words: What, How old, Where.

📘 Language bank
Greetings: Hello, Hi, Good morning, Good afternoon, Good evening.
Goodbyes: Goodbye, Bye, See you later, Good night.
Politeness: please, thank you, you're welcome, Nice to meet you, excuse me, sorry.
Personal information: name, age, country, city, nationality, job, phone number.
Useful sentences: What's your name? / How old are you? / Where are you from? / I'm from Tunisia. / Nice to meet you.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Choose the correct word.
1. (Hi / Good night) Sami! How are you?
2. Good morning. What (is / are) your name?
3. How old (is / are) you?
4. Where (do / are) you from?
5. Nice to (meet / meeting) you.

Exercise 2 — Complete the dialogue.
A: Good morning. What's your ______ ?
B: My ______ is Mariem.
A: How ______ are you?
B: I ______ twelve years old.
A: Where are you ______ ?
B: I'm ______ Sousse.

Exercise 3 — Correct the mistake.
1. I have twelve years.
2. She is name Nour.
3. Where you are from?
4. My name Karim.
5. He are from Gabès.

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. Hi 2. is 3. are 4. are 5. meet.
Exercise 2: name / name / old / am / from / from.
Exercise 3: 1. I am twelve (years old). 2. Her name is Nour. 3. Where are you from? 4. My name is Karim. 5. He is from Gabès.

🗣️ Speaking task
Stand up and introduce yourself to three classmates. Say hello, give your name, your age and where you are from, then finish with "Nice to meet you." Listen carefully and remember one piece of information about each person.

👀 Extra note
Two mistakes to avoid forever:
1. Age uses "to be", not "to have": I AM twelve (never I have twelve).
2. Every sentence about personal information needs the verb "to be": I AM from Tunisia, my name IS Karim, she IS eleven. If you can hear am / is / are in the sentence, you are usually on the right track.

📋 Summary
- Choose your greeting depending on who you talk to: informal (Hi, Hello) with friends; formal (Good morning/afternoon/evening) with teachers and adults.
- "Good night" is only for saying goodbye at night, never a greeting.
- A full self-introduction follows five steps: greet, give your name, your age, where you're from, then close politely ("Nice to meet you").
- The verb "to be" is essential for personal information: I am, you/we/they are, he/she/it is (contractions: I'm, you're, he's...).
- Negative forms: I'm not, isn't, aren't. Questions: Am I...? Is he...? Are they...?
- Age always uses "to be" (I am twelve), never "to have" (never "I have twelve years").
- Question words for personal information: What (name), How old (age), Where (place, origin).
- Capital letters are always required for names, countries and languages: Tunisia, Karim, English.

Read the identity cards of two pupils.
| Name | Age | City |
|---|---|---|
| Mehdi | 13 | Sfax |
| Lina | 12 | Bizerte |

1) You are Mehdi. Answer the question: How old are you?
2) You are Lina. Answer the same question.
3) Complete: Mehdi ______ thirteen years old.
4) Choose the correct sentence: I have thirteen years. / I am thirteen years old.
Complete: Where are you ___? — I am from Tunisia.
Give a formal greeting in the morning.

Read the dialogue at the school library.
Librarian: Good morning. What's your name?
Pupil: My name is Yassine Trabelsi.
Librarian: How do you spell your first name?
Pupil: ______

Answer the questions.
1) Write the pupil's answer: spell the name Yassine letter by letter.
2) Spell the family name Trabelsi in the same way.
3) Write the question we ask when we want to know the spelling of a word.
4) Now spell your own first name.

It is nine o'clock in the evening. Amine is at his friend Omar's house. Now he wants to go home.
Amine: It's late. I must go now. ______, Omar!
Omar: ______, Amine. See you tomorrow at school!

1) Choose the two correct expressions to complete the dialogue: Good morning / Goodbye / Good night / Hello.
2) Put each expression in the right group (when we arrive / when we leave): Hi, Bye, Good evening, See you later.
3) Write what you say to your mother before you go to bed.

A new pupil, Farah, meets a classmate. There is one mistake in each of the classmate's questions.
Classmate: Hello! What is you name?
Farah: My name is Farah.
Classmate: And what is you family name?
Farah: It's Gharbi.
Classmate: Where is you house?
Farah: It's near the school.

1) Find the wrong word in the three questions.
2) Rewrite the three questions correctly.
3) Complete: “you” is a subject pronoun; “______” is a possessive adjective and it comes before a noun.

Two friends meet in the street.
Salim: Hi, Nader! How ______ you?
Nader: I ______ fine, thanks. And you?
Salim: I'm very well, thank you. How ______ your mother?
Nader: She ______ fine too.

1) Complete the dialogue with am, is or are.
2) Give another answer to the question “How are you?”.
3) Write the full form of: I'm.
4) Match each subject with its verb. Subjects: I, you, she. Verbs: is, am, are.

Read the dialogue at a family party.
Mr Jones: Good evening. My name is Tom Jones.
Mrs Karoui: Nice to meet you. I'm Leila Karoui.
Mr Jones: ______?
Mrs Karoui: I'm a doctor. I work in a hospital.

1) Write the missing question about Mrs Karoui's job. Give two possible forms.
2) Match each job with its place. Jobs: doctor, teacher, farmer. Places: school, farm, hospital.
3) Complete with a or an: She is ______ doctor. He is ______ engineer.
4) Ask your friend the same question about his or her father.
